newsitem.title: INDONESIA: A chronology of recent history of East Timor.
newsitem.headline: A chronology of recent history of East Timor.

text.p: A chronology of the recent history in the former Portuguese colony of East Timor, incorporated by Indonesia as its 27th province.
April 25 - Armed forces coup in Lisbon leads to overthrow of Caetano regime and move for Portugal to withdraw from most of its colonies.
August 27 - Portuguese governor and administration withdraw from East Timor capital Dili to offshore island of Atauro.
Nov 28 - After brief civil war, left-wing Revolutionary Front for the Independent East Timor (Fretilin) declares East Timor independent.

Nov 29 - In presence of leaders of Timorese Democratic Union (UDT) and Timorese Popular Democratic Association (Apodeti), Indonesian Foreign Minister Adam Malik signs declaration integrating territory into Indonesia.
Dec 7 - Indonesian troops invade East Timor.
July 17 - President Suharto signs a bill formally declaring East Timor Indonesia's 27th province. United Nations does not recognise this and says Portugal remains administering power.

Nov 3 - U.N. General Assembly instructs secretary-general to initiate consultations with all parties concerned on East Timor. By 1996, no progress has been made in U.S.-sponsored talks between Indonesia and Portugal.
Salesian priest Carlos Felipe Ximenes Belo, who has been out of East Timor for most of the time since Indonesian invasion, is appointed Apostolic Administrator of East Timor.
Feb 6 - Bishop Belo writes to U.N. Secretary-General Perez de Cuellar calling for referendum on East Timor's future.
Oct 12 - Pope John Paul II visits mostly Catholic East Timor and celebrates mass before 100,000 people in Dili.

Nov 12 - Indonesian troops open fire on procession on way to Dili's Santa Cruz cemetary after funeral for shot anti- Indonesian activist, killing by official accounts 50 people. Human rights groups estimate number killed at least 180.
Nov 20 - Leader of East Timor's armed resistance Xanana Gusmao captured, convicted May 21, 1993, of subversion and sentenced to life in prison, later commuted to 20 years.
July 20 - Indonesian government gives go ahead for talks between pro- and anti-integration East Timorese; series of talks subsequently held but without producing resolution to problem.

Nov 12 - Twenty-nine East Timorese students enter U.S. embassy compound during Asian-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum meeting in Jakarta attended by President Bill Clinton. Clinton subsequently brings up human rights issue with President Suharto at bilateral meeting.

Jan 12 - Indonesian troops kill six civilians after Fretilin attack in which one soldier was wounded. Indonesian government subsequently announces military enquiry discovers "an action by military personnel...not based on proper procedure". Disciplinary action taken against soldiers involved.
Late in 1995 and in 1996, a number of East Timorese enter foreign embassies in Jakarta seeking political asylum. Most are sent on to Portugal.
Oct 11 - Belo and self-exiled resistance spokesman Jose Ramos Horta jointly awarded Nobel Peace prize, causing suprise and anger among many Indonesians.

Nov 12 - Students stage brief protest in front of University of East Timor. Youth members of Indonesia's ruling Golkar party call in Jakarta for expulsion of Belo over German magazine interview in which he was quoted as saying military treated East Timorese "like dogs".
